question: Natural rubber is soft at high temperatures and brittle at low temperatures; hence raw rubber is heated with sulphur and other additives at a temperature range between 373 – 415 K to make it strong. This process is called ______ of rubber.
solution:
The correct answer is __vulcanisation**(option 2)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Vulcanisation__ is a chemical process that improves the physical properties of rubber.
 
• Raw rubber is heated with sulphur and additives at a temperature range of 373–415 K during vulcanisation.
 
• This process makes the rubber stronger, more elastic, and resistant to temperature changes.
 
• It prevents rubber from becoming brittle at low temperatures and too soft at high temperatures.
 
• Charles Goodyear is credited with the discovery of vulcanisation in the 19th century.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Molding:**

 
 
• Molding is a manufacturing process where rubber is shaped into specific forms using molds.
 
• It does not enhance the strength or elasticity of the material like vulcanisation does.
 
 
 
• **Extrusion:**
 
 
• Extrusion involves forcing rubber through a die to create specific shapes.
 
• It is a forming process and not related to improving the material's properties like vulcanisation.
 
 
 
• **Latex:**
 
 
• Latex is the natural liquid form of rubber obtained from rubber trees.
 
• It requires further processing, including vulcanisation, to transform into usable rubber products.
